title: Echo
intro: Walk east until the wall, then north [i]the same distance[/i], then step into the exit on your right. The decoy pockets look exactly like the exit, you have no variables, and you can't afford to peek into every pocket.
cs_note: Each pending function call is a [b]stack frame[/b]. If A moves and then calls itself, every step east leaves a frame waiting; when the calls return, each frame replays one move north. The call stack is memory.
hints: A function can call itself. What should A do when the way ahead is blocked? That's the base case.
Inside A: if path_ahead(), then move(), A(), move(). Otherwise turn_left(). That's the whole function.

Each call of A takes one step east, then waits on the [b]call stack[/b] with one move() still to do. At the wall, the base case turns left. Now every waiting call finishes its second move(), heading north: exactly as many steps as you went east. Main then turns right and steps into the exit.
